summary: Peter Gaeffke (1927–2005) was an Indologist. He studied at Regensburg, Mainz (PhD 1952), and the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies. He held positions at Mainz, Utrecht University (Professor 1964), and the University of Pennsylvania (1972; Professor 1975–2003).
Peter Gyallay-Pap works in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the London School of Economics in 1990 and served as an adjunct at Adams State University (attested 2007).

Peter Harvey is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies in 1996 and served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Sunderland (attested 2002–2015).
Peter Haskel is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He was a graduate student at Columbia University, where he studied under Yoshito S. Hakeda.

Peter J. Wilson (1933–2005) completed his Ph.D. at Yale University (~1957–1961). He taught at Yale (~1961–1964), Vassar College, the University of Washington (~1965–1970), Bennington College, and the University of Otago (~1971–1998).

Peter James Gilks is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and completed a PhD at the Australian National University (attested 2010) under John Powers, among several traditional teachers.
Peter K. Austin (born 1952) is a linguist who studied at the Australian National University (1975–1978). He held a post at SOAS University of London (~2002–2018).

Peter Koret works in Buddhist studies and linguistics. He completed his doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London and has held posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.

Peter Kornicki (born 1950) is a scholar of Japanology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Oxford (MSc, DPhil) and Tokyo, he taught at the University of Tasmania, Kyoto University, Robinson College, and Cambridge (~1985–2017).

Peter Kuhlmann (born 1965) is a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He completed his doctorate under Rosemarie Lühr (~1990–1993) and held posts at the University of Giessen, University of Düsseldorf, and University of Göttingen.

Peter M. Scharf (born 1957) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He wrote his dissertation at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona, and also studied with Shrinarayan Mishra, Ludo Rocher, and Narendranath Pandey.
Peter Masefield is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under supervisors L. P. N. Perera and Ninian Smart (attested 1986).

Peter Moran is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Tufts University and the University of Washington (PhD), supervised by Charles Keyes, and studied under multiple traditional and academic teachers.

Peter N. Gregory (born 1945) works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at Harvard (1981) under Masatoshi Nagatomi and held posts at UIUC, the Kuroda Institute, Komazawa University, and Smith College.

Peter Schreiner (born 1945) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Educated at Temple, Münster (PhD), and Tübingen (Habilitation), he held posts at Tübingen, SOAS (1988), and the University of Zurich (1990).
Peter Schwabland is a scholar in the field of Tibetology. He earned his MA at the University of Washington, where he studied under Leonard van der Kuijp.

Peter Schwieger (born 1952) is a Tibetologist. He earned his doctorate and Habilitation at the University of Bonn under Dieter Schuh, and held posts at the Göttingen Academy, Humboldt University, and the University of Bonn (2001).

Peter Skilling is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his PhD at the EPHE under Cristina Scherrer-Schaub. He founded the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation and has held posts at EFEO, Chulalongkorn, and multiple visiting professorships.

Peter Stewart (born 1971), a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Clare College, Cambridge (PhD). He held posts at Cambridge, Reading, the Courtauld Institute, and Oxford (from 2011), where he directed CARC.

Peter Zieme (born 1942) is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, linguistic, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Humboldt University, he worked at the GDR Academy of Sciences, BBAW's Turfanforschung, and Free University of Berlin.
